title: microquota-anchoring-heuristics-notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a lightweight scratchpad exploring small-quota / microquota pricing patterns for interactive LLM features (chat widgets, in-app assistants). Goal: an experimentable set of anchoring heuristics that balance perceived generosity, conversion into paid plans, and unit economics for short, high-frequency sessions. Keep the heuristics simple so product can A/B them easily.

Problems we're solving:
- Free tier usage hogging tokens for a tiny cohort (power users)
- Per-session pricing is confusing for non-technical PMs and customers
- Need simple anchor numbers for marketing and UX to communicate limits
- Want to preserve predictability for median usage while allowing exploratory bursts

Design constraints and assumptions (back-of-envelope):
- Hosted cost baseline: $0.000004 per 1 token served (hosted blend; mix of small/medium models) — round numbers for thinking.
- Median session length for product widget: 120 user tokens + 180 model tokens = 300 tokens total per session.
- High-value session (power user): 2,000 tokens.
- Conversion target: free -> paid conversion uplift if free allowance covers ~3 sessions / week for average user.

Microquota primitives to consider:
1) Session-credits: give N credits per month; 1 credit = 1 session up to 400 tokens (capped). Extra tokens consumed outside cap billed per-token or consume additional fractional credits.
2) Token-bucket allowance: monthly token cap with soft refill every 24 hrs (time-decay refill).
3) Burst credits: small ephemeral credits given on sign-up or as referral reward; expire in 14 days.
4) Usage bands: small free band (0-5k tokens/month), mid band (5k-50k), above that convert to reserved or metered pricing.

Anchoring heuristics (UX friendly numbers):
- Free starter: 10 session-credits / month (assume 300 tokens per session -> ~3k tokens). Anchor text: “~10 short chats per month”
- Trial upgrade credit: +50 burst credits valid for 14 days (good for ~15 typical sessions)
- Micro paid plan: $9/mo for 100 session-credits (~30k tokens), caps at 400 tokens/session; effective cost to user per session = $0.09.

Unit economics (rough):
- Cost per token = $0.000004 -> cost per typical session (300 tokens) = $0.0012. That’s tiny vs price.
- For micro paid plan: $9 / 100 sessions = $0.09 revenue per session. Gross margin per session = 0.09 - 0.0012 ~= $0.0888 (>98%).
- Breakeven if heavy sessions: if users do 2000 token sessions, cost = 2000 * 0.000004 = $0.008 -> still << $0.09. So simple session-credits look extremely profitable at current cost assumptions.

Risks & behavioral considerations:
- Users may game session-credits by splitting/concatenating prompts to stay under cap; need a clear definition of session boundaries (client-side cookie + server heuristics).
- High-precision apps (long-form writing assistants) will find session-credit UX clumsy; target microquota at short interactive features.
- Perceived fairness: if starter allows 10 sessions but each session can be 2k tokens, users can consume a lot. Enforce per-session soft cap (e.g., 400 tokens) on free credits.

Experiment matrix (A/B ideas):
A: Free: 10 session credits/month + 400 token/session cap. B: Free: 3k tokens/month (no per-session cap). Metric: conversion rate to paid within 30 days, median session length, churn.
C: Display remaining "sessions this month" vs "tokens remaining" wording — measure NPS and comprehension in user tests.
D: Offer micro paid plan ($4/mo) for 50 sessions with higher per-session cap (800 tokens) — see uplift vs $9/mo plan.

Edge pricing knobs (to tune):
- Token cap per session (400 vs 800)
- Session credit price (anchor at $0.05, $0.09, $0.15)
- Burst credit generosity and expiry (7d vs 14d)
- Soft refill rate (daily refill of 1 credit vs weekly refill)

Math helpers / quick formulas (for product to use):
- tokens_per_session_estimate = user_tokens + model_tokens (we often use 0.6*model_tokens to reflect assistant verbosity but put raw numbers in UX)
- effective_cost_per_session = tokens_per_session_estimate * cost_per_token
- plan_unit_cost = plan_price / included_sessions
- margin_per_session = plan_unit_cost - effective_cost_per_session

Example sims (table-style bullets):
- Free user (10 session credits): if median user uses 8 sessions -> 8 * 300 = 2400 tokens/month. Host cost ~= $0.0096/month. Cheap.
- Power free user (10 sessions at 2k tokens each): 20k tokens -> cost = $0.08/month. Still very small; indicates free allowance could be generous without breaking economics.
- Conversion case: Assume 1,000 DAUs sign up, 10% convert to micro paid at $9/mo -> 100 * 9 = $900/mo. Host cost for 100 converters doing avg 20 sessions/month: 100 * 20 * 300 * 0.000004 = $2.4/mo. Clean unit economics.

Operational considerations / policy language:
- Define session start: first user message after 15 mins of inactivity or new browser session. Store session id for counting credits.
- Hard per-session enforcement only on free and micro plans; enterprise and dedicated customers will have different rules.
- Rate limit vs credit consumption: Credits reduce, but also enforce request throughput caps to avoid spikes.

Open questions / next actions:
- Need accurate cost_per_token estimate from infra finance for our 2025 model mix (quantized LoRA vs full fp16) — current 0.000004 is optimistic.
- UX: sketch copy options for "10 short chats a month" vs "3k tokens a month" and paper-test with 20 users.
- Build small telemetry dashboard: sessions/month per free user, tokens/session distribution, top 1% token consumers. Link to RD-7342 to track.
- Run A/B on 5k users for 30 days; primary metric: paid conversion at 30 days. Secondary: average token consumption, support tickets.

Notes to self:
- If infra cost jumps x5, micro plans still look viable but top-heavy free allowances will need pruning.
- Consider hybrid: give both session-credits and token cushion (e.g., 10 sessions + 1k token cushion) to reduce edge cases.

Quick copy mock for marketing: "Starter: 10 free short chats every month — perfect for trying our assistant. Upgrade to Micro for $9/mo and get 100 chats + longer responses."

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after cost numbers and a quick UX test with PMs.
